assessment: The incumbent provides embedded-caption previews and accessible history. It achieved the timing target in 20/30 sessions, below the required 27/30. H1-O3, O4 and O5 support a hypothesis that completion ordering and weakly retained input associations contribute to unexpected versions; they do not distinguish incorrect render inputs from incorrect preview selection. H1-O7 limits a blanket rendering explanation: nine single-correction sessions succeeded in five to 11 minutes without reported uncertainty. H1-O6 establishes sampled usage, not festival capacity. All evidence is stipulated synthetic data.

openings.claim: Hypothesis: bind each render request to an immutable video-and-caption pair, and show that same pair identity when requesting, browsing and downloading a preview.
openings.delta: Replace reliance on completion numbers and external filename reconstruction with a persistent input association, retaining the last delivered pair and original caption wording.
openings.prediction: Under deliberately reversed completion order, downloaded previews match their selected pair's hashes and editors select their intended pair with fewer corrections.
openings.probe: In private staging, replay overlapping requests using demonstration footage and two caption versions. Verify input/output associations and observe editor selection. Bound implementation to the stipulated effort and retain the existing renderer and delivery format; reject expansion beyond that allowance.
assumptions: Inputs can be retained immutably on existing accounts within four engineer-days and current computing allowance.
Pair labels convey enough meaning for editors to recognize intent.

openings.claim: Do delayed sessions lose most time before the intended pair is ready, or after it is available?
openings.delta: Separate processing delay from identification and inspection delay before choosing the next intervention.
openings.prediction: If history interpretation dominates, delayed sessions show long post-availability intervals and repeated selections; if rendering dominates, most excess time precedes availability. Single-correction sessions provide a limiting comparison.
openings.probe: Align timestamped render events with bounded editor replays recording final edit, intended-pair availability, selection and completed inspection; compare overlapping-request and single-correction cases within one editor-day.
assumptions: Replays approximate real selection behavior; historical render events alone cannot reconstruct attention.
